title: The Endless Bell
premise: Ulyana Crane takes a teaching post in the fog-bound village of Hollowmere, where children have been vanishing from her classroom one at a time, and the villagers insist they never existed. The village's church bell, melted down in 1911 after a fire that killed eleven pupils, begins to ring at dusk — once for each child the village still owes. Ulyana realizes the missing students are being 'counted' by something that remembers what the village chose to forget: a century-old cover-up of a schoolmaster's crimes, sustained by every family since. To save her remaining students — including her own daughter, whose existence no record supports — she must publicly name the dead and force the village to hear its own history before the bell finishes counting. In the end, the bell falls silent only when Ulyana sacrifices her carefully constructed false identity, confessing who she really is: the granddaughter of the schoolmaster's last victim.
about_author: Mirabel Pemberton is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in coastal villages where old churches outnumbered residents. They write horror about institutions that protect themselves at any cost, and dedicate each book to a student whose name was never entered in the register.

chapters.title: The Register of Small Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives in Hollowmere and takes over a class of nine children, though enrollment records list fourteen. The headmaster, Mr. Aldous Vane, is charmingly evasive about the discrepancy. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: quiet unease masked by professional optimism; she has learned not to ask questions.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: A boy named Tam fails to arrive; his desk is gone by afternoon, and classmates deny he ever existed. Ulyana finds Tam's name scratched into her desk's underside. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: gaslit self-doubt — twelve years of practiced rationalization begin to crack.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: In the village archive, Ulyana reads of the 1911 schoolhouse fire that killed eleven pupils, after which the church bell was melted down. The schoolmaster, Edmund Grieve, was praised as a hero. POV: Ulyana with an intercut 1911 diary fragment. Emotional beat: dread hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Bell at Dusk
chapters.summary: The melted bell rings once across the empty churchyard. Only Ulyana and a mute groundskeeper, Ilsa, seem to hear it. Ilsa presses a scrap of bell-metal into Ulyana's hand. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: terror breaking through denial; the supernatural is now undeniable.

chapters.title: Nine Little Counters
chapters.summary: The bell rings twice; another child, Wren, is erased overnight. The surviving children begin whispering a counting rhyme about the bell. Ulyana confronts Vane, who warns her that families here keep their own justice. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: isolation — the village closes ranks around her.

chapters.title: Grieve's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the sealed cellar beneath the school, Ulyana finds Grieve's ledger: names of children he abused, and proof the fire was the villagers' revenge — and that they burned the wrong man's evidence along with the children. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; the victims' justice became a new crime.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ulyana's daughter Maren appears on no register, and the bell has begun ringing toward her count. Ulyana admits to herself why she came: Maren is the descendant Grieve's line still owes. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: maternal fear fused with guilt over her years of hiding.

chapters.title: Vigil of the Forgiven
chapters.summary: The villagers hold a festival honoring Grieve while the bell tolls seven times. Ulyana tries to flee with Maren but the road loops back to Hollowmere; the village will not release what it refuses to remember. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair — escape is impossible without truth.

chapters.title: The Counting
chapters.summary: Climax. On the fire's anniversary, the bell rings ten times and the erased children manifest in the schoolroom, waiting. Ulyana drags the whole village inside, reads Grieve's ledger aloud, and names every victim — ending with her grandmother's name and her own true one. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cathartic confrontation; truth as exorcism.

chapters.title: Silence, Entered in Full
chapters.summary: The bell cracks and falls silent; the children are remembered, their names restored to stone and register. Hollowmere must live with its history unhidden. Ulyana stays as teacher under her real name, Maren enrolled at last. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — identity reclaimed through memory, justice outside the law finally answered by witness.
